title: Duchy of Parma and Piacenza
capsule: The Duchy of Parma and Piacenza was restored at the Congress of Vienna in 1815 and assigned to Marie Louise of Austria, Napoleon's former empress, under whose able administration it prospered until her death in 1847 returned it to the Bourbon-Parma line under Carlo II. The duchy was drawn into the Italian revolutionary upheavals of 1848–49 and, after Austrian defeat at Solferino (June 1859), a popular assembly voted in August 1859 for annexation to Piedmont-Sardinia. It was formally incorporated into the Kingdom of Sardinia in March 1860 and became part of the unified Kingdom of Italy the following year.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's boundaries in the Po valley are well-documented from the Congress of Vienna acts through Italian unification records; some border adjustments with neighbouring Italian states are less precisely mapped.
